elements.id-string-8: Recent advancements in charmoniumlike state have significantly enriched the discovery of new hadronic states, providing exciting opportunities for further investigations into the fascinating realm of charmonium physics.
elements.id-string-9: In this letter, we focus on the vector charmonium family and perform a detailed analysis of the recently observed $e^+e^-\to \pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ process.
elements.id-string-10: Our findings demonstrate a striking agreement between the observed peak structures and the predicted characterized energy level structure of higher vector charmonia including the $\psi(4220)$, $\psi(4380)$, $\psi(4415)$, and $\psi(4500)$, which are derived from an unquenched potential model.
elements.id-string-11: This discovery challenges conventional understanding of higher charmonia above 4 GeV and offers fresh insights into the dynamics of charm and anti-charm quarks in the formation of these states.
elements.id-string-12: Furthermore, the identification of these higher charmonia in the precisely measured $\pi^+ D^0D^{*-}$ open-charm decay channel would serve as compelling evidence supporting the unquenched scenario and contribute to a deeper understanding of the nonperturbative aspects of the strong interaction.
elements.id-string-13: {\it{Introduction}}.---As we enter the 21st century, higher precision experiments have yielded a plethora of surprising and promising results in hadron spectroscopy.
elements.id-string-14: Notably, a series of new hadronic states, such as the charmoniumlike $XYZ$ and $P_c$ states, have been discovered \cite{ParticleDataGroup:2020ssz,Chen:2016qju,Liu:2019zoy,Chen:2022asf,Guo:2017jvc,Olsen:2017bmm,Brambilla:2019esw}.
elements.id-string-15: This marks the onset of a new phase of hadron spectroscopy research, which may provide valuable insights into the nonperturbative problem of the strong interaction, a long-standing puzzle in particle physics.
elements.id-string-16: In the 1970s, the observation of the $J/\psi$ particle \cite{E598:1974sol,SLAC-SP-017:1974ind} introduced a new class of hadrons known as charmonium.
elements.id-string-17: Subsequently, experimentalists discovered numerous charmonium states, which now constitute the bulk of charmonium cataloged by the Particle Data Group (PDG) \cite{ParticleDataGroup:2020ssz}.
elements.id-string-18: Moreover, these observations of charmonium stimulated the development of the Cornell model with the linear plus Coulomb potential, a quenched potential model proposed by Eichten {\it et al.} \cite{Eichten:1974af,Eichten:1978tg}.
elements.id-string-19: This model has inspired various potential models, including  famous Godfrey-Isgur (GI) model \cite{Godfrey:1985xj}, which facilitates quantitative calculations of hadron spectroscopy.
elements.id-string-20: Although substantial progress has been made in the field of hadron spectroscopy, it is important to note that our current understanding of it is not yet complete.
elements.id-string-21: In particular, establishing the energy level structure of higher charmonium states above 4.2 GeV has remained a challenge for several decades since the discovery of the $J/\psi$.
elements.id-string-22: In 2014, the Lanzhou group drew attention to the striking similarity between the charmonium and bottomonium families \cite{He:2014xna}.
elements.id-string-23: They determined the mass of the narrow-width charmonium state $\psi(4S)$ to be 4263 MeV, which is markedly different from the conventional assignment of $\psi(4415)$ as the $\psi(4S)$ under quenched potential models such as the Cornell model \cite{Eichten:1974af,Eichten:1978tg}.
elements.id-string-24: However, this result is consistent with the expectations from the screening potential \cite{Dong:1994zj,Li:2009zu}.
elements.id-string-25: Soon after, the BESIII Collaboration surprised us with the discovery of narrow structures around 4.2 GeV referred to as the $Y(4220)$ in processes involving $e^+e^-$ annihilations into hidden-charm channels, such as $J/\psi\pi^+\pi^-$ \cite{BESIII:2016bnd}, $h_c\pi^+\pi^-$ \cite{BESIII:2016adj}, $\omega\chi_{c0}$ \cite{BESIII:2019gjc}, and $\psi(3686)\pi^+\pi^-$ \cite{BESIII:2017tqk}.
elements.id-string-26: These observations were consistent with the expectation that there is a charmonium state, the $\psi(4220)$ \cite{Chen:2014sra}.
elements.id-string-27: Taking this opportunity, researchers realized the potential of the observed $Y(4220)$ narrow structure as a scaling point for constructing the energy level structure of higher charmonia above 4.2 GeV in Ref.
elements.id-string-29: By using an unquenched potential model, the $Y(4220)$ was assigned to the charmonium family under the $4S$-$3D$ mixing scheme, and its charmonium partner $\psi(4380)$ was predicted \cite{Wang:2019mhs}.
elements.id-string-30: During this process, the well-established $\psi(4415)$ was proposed as a $5S$-$4D$ mixing state, while its charmonium partner $\psi(4500)$ was also found to exist \cite{Wang:2019mhs,Wang:2022jxj}.
elements.id-string-31: As a result, a characterized energy level structure for higher vector charmonia above 4.2 GeV has been obtained under an unquenched potential model.
elements.id-string-32: Given this research background, identifying this predicted higher charmonium energy level structure in its open-charm decay channels has become a critical step in the entire study.
elements.id-string-33: Open-charm decay channels are known to dominate the widths of higher charmonia, and their contributions may provide crucial evidence to test such a scenario.
elements.id-string-34: In recent years, the BESIII Collaboration has made significant progress in measuring the $e^+e^-$ annihilation processes into open-charm channels \cite{BESIII:2018iea,BESIII:2021yvc,BESIII:2022quc,BESIII:2023cmv,BESIII:2023wsc}.
elements.id-string-35: In this letter, it is reported that the peak structures observed in the newly observed $e^+e^-\to \pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ process match well with the characterized energy level structure of higher vector charmonia predicted by the unquenched potential model, which includes the $\psi(4220)$, $\psi(4380)$, $\psi(4415)$, and $\psi(4500)$ states.
elements.id-string-36: This finding challenges our long-held perception of higher charmonia above 4 GeV and sheds new light on how charm and anti-charm quarks interact to form these states.
elements.id-string-37: The identification of these key higher charmonia in the $\pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ open-charm decay channel not only provides crucial evidence to test the unquenched scenario but also enriches our understanding of the nonperturbative aspects of the strong interaction.
elements.id-string-38: {\it The emergence of the charmonium structures with characterized energy level in $e^+e^-\to \pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$}.---In recent decades, the discovery of various charmoniumlike $XYZ$ states has brought attention to the significant role of the unquenched effect in the color confinement potential \cite{Chen:2016qju}.
elements.id-string-39: Building upon these advancements, we have directed our attention to the challenging charmoniumlike $Y$ problem, offering a promising solution framework through the implementation of an unquenched quark potential model, as detailed in our previous work \cite{Wang:2019mhs}.

elements.id-string-145: This letter aims to address the long-standing challenge of constructing the higher vector charmonium family above 4 GeV.
elements.id-string-146: By analyzing the open-charm process $e^+e^-\to \pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ in detail, we reveal a remarkable agreement between the observed enhancement structures and the characterized energy level structure predicted by the unquenched potential model.
elements.id-string-147: The identified states, including $\psi(4220)$, $\psi(4380)$, $\psi(4415)$, and $\psi(4500)$, challenge conventional understanding and offer new insights into the dynamics of charm and anti-charm quarks in their formation.
elements.id-string-148: By overcoming multiple solution problems arising from resonance interference in the cross section analysis, we can further facilitate identification of characterized energy level structures of higher vector charmonia by comparing them with theoretical predictions of the three-body  $\pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ decay behaviors.
elements.id-string-149: By utilizing the effective decay amplitude, the calculated three-body decay behaviors of $\psi \to \pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ sheds light on the properties of higher vector charmonia, particularly confirming the significant contribution of $\psi(4380)$ in the $e^+e^- \to\pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ process.
elements.id-string-150: Collectively, these findings provide strong evidence for the existence of the characterized energy level structure of higher vector charmonia.
elements.id-string-151: This work deepens our understanding of charmonium physics, emphasizing the need for precise experimental measurements of $e^+e^- \to\pi^+ D^0 D^{*-}$ to further advance the study of charmonium spectroscopy above 4.0 GeV.
